summary: A brick pier light at Fairport Harbor, lit in 1925 after a shell was built ashore and floated out; its keepers, its 1948 automation, and its private owner since 2011.

structures.note: Brick in steel frame, square; base to lantern centre 42 ft (USLHS). Shell fabricated at the Buffalo depot and moved to the site in 1921.
Keeper's quarters attached to the tower (USLHS); the 1921 shell was built ashore and transferred to the breakwater

access.note: Privately owned since the 2011 auction sale; lighthouse closed to visitors. LighthouseFriends describes the grounds as open; treat the house and land as private.

facts.agency: Private owner since 2011 (formerly U.S. Coast Guard)

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends reports the Coast Guard sold the light at auction and the 2011 buyer took private ownership; the restoration site describes a private renovation.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives 1925 because that is when the light was completed and first lit. The steel shell was built ashore and set on the pier in 1921 (Bulletin 1921), and the tower and lantern were finished for the 1925 light.

notes_for_editor:
Sources. The NRHP nomination (NRIS 92000242) is a 22 KB 'not yet digitized' placeholder; the story uses only the NPGallery metadata (listing date). No Board or Commissioner report after 1901 is in the local corpus, so the 1911-1925 construction history rests on LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Service Bulletin. The Bulletin's 1921 text printed 'Fairport Harbor, N. Y.' in one place; the story does not use it. The 1921 Bulletin's OCR reads '38t feet' for the tower height, which LighthouseFriends prints as 38 1/2 feet; the story gives 38 1/2 feet and cites both.

Ownership and privacy. The 2009-2011 auction bidders and the 2011 buyer are not named in the story; the buyer is described only by her public role as a marketing executive, as LighthouseFriends reports. The LaRose and Brophy details are the keepers' public service records. Personal family details in LighthouseFriends are left out.

Links. The LaRose line and his other_stations entries rest on the Digital Archive's own person record (archives.uslhs.org/people/frank-larose), which lists Conneaut Harbor West Breakwater as first assistant (1917-1920 and 1920-1927), Fairport Harbor (old stone light) and Fairport Harbor West Breakwater as principal (both 1927-1937), and South Bass Island as principal (1937-1941). The two 1927-1937 principal entries overlap; LighthouseFriends mentions only the breakwater light for those years. An earlier draft of this record gave the old Fairport Harbor post as 1920-1927; the person record does not say that. No id is given for Conneaut: check whether a station record covers it. Brophy's Ashtabula service (about 1932-1937) rests on LighthouseFriends alone and is marked approximate.

Record checks. The record's characteristic (Iso W 6s) and range (11.3 nm) were not verified: no Light List was read. LighthouseFriends gives the 1925 characteristic as occulting white every five seconds; whether it is the same now is not confirmed. The lens history (fourth-order Fresnel removed, date not given) has no source for a removal date, so no lens_removed event is recorded. Automation has no date in LighthouseFriends; 1948 comes from the roster's last keeper and the website.

Other stations. The Life-Saving Service's Fairport station (1876-1878 entries in the LSS reports) is a separate station and is not used here. The old stone Fairport Harbor light (us-oh-fairport-harbor) is cross-referenced only.
